newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian MTBE - Softer on Bangchak award, lack of demand.
newsitem.headline: Asian MTBE - Softer on Bangchak award, lack of demand.

text.p: Asian MTBE prices softened on a lack of demand and the low Bangchak award but a floor to the fall is expected ahead of the U.S. driving season, industry sources said on Wednesday.
Free-on-board (fob) Singapore MTBE lifting April was assessed around at $265-$270 per tonne, compared to offers last week at $270-$272 per tonne.
Some fob material was sold at over $270 last week, but the trade was before Thai refiner Bangchak Petroleum Plc awarded its April 16-30 delivery tender which closed March 19.
Bangchak bought 1,500 tonnes of MTBE from Saudi Basic Industries Corp (SABIC) between $270-$275 per tonne c-and-f Thailand, around $10 lower than its previous tender for its March requirements.
"It is always very low...it is not an indication but it could pull the market down," said one producer.
On a netback to Singapore fob prices, the Bangchak award translates to around $250, traders said.
"The feedstock methanol is nearly the same (price) as MTBE then," said a producer.

Due to weaker MTBE prices and rising prices of propylene, a Malaysian MTBE producer has switched its production to favour the basic petrochemical building block rather than the gasoline blending component, industry sources said.

The plant which normally produces 900 to 1,000 tonnes per day of 100-percent MTBE, has been in "high propylene mode" since January, cutting its MTBE output by 70-80 percent and producing 8000,000 tonnes of propylene a year.

"It is much better to run on propylene mode -- supplies are tight, prices are very firm and are increasing every week by around $10 to $20 (per tonne)," a trader said. "It went past the $500 range a couple of weeks ago, and is now in the $600s."
Market sources however said MTBE prices would bottom out as it has been rangebound since July last year between $260-$280, and even rise as the summer driving season approaches.
"It has been very, very quiet with no enquiries for spot cargoes," said a producer. "But in the last week we did receive some enquiries for the U.S. market but for May."
Traders said the arbitrage to the U.S. did not currently work -- a $20 difference is required to open the window.
"But we hope to see the price increasing in the U.S. to prepare for the summer," the producer said.
"The black cloud is SABIC's Sadaf plant," a producer said on the 700,000-tonne-per-year Saudi plant, a 50:50 joint-venture between SABIC and the Royal Dutch Shell due to startup in April.

The next market indicator will be Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp's (CPC) import tender for 3,500 to 7,000 tonnes of MTBE for May 6-20 delivery to Kaohsiung and Keelung which closes March 31 and is valid until April 2.
In its last MTBE tender, CPC bought 7,000 tonnes for April 6-20 delivery from SABIC at $280-$283 per tonne c-and-f Kaohsiung and Keelung.
